purpose: Qualify or reject a physical-event evidence certificate without reusing operational ledgers as the final adjudicator.

minimumRig.physicalEvent: One relay edge that produces a separately measurable shaft, optical, or electrical transition.

calibrationBeforeFaultInjection.gate: Do not run the confirmation matrix if uncertainty intervals overlap the zero/one/two-event decision regions or if witness dependence is not bounded.

faultMatrix.cut: after command persistence before actuator acceptance
during physical transition before W1 retention
after W1 retention before W2 retention

faultMatrix.partition: both asymmetric directions in separate runs

independence.development: Controller and operational ledger may be used to construct the rig and inject faults.
independence.adjudication: A separate implementation receives only sealed witness bundles, calibration artifacts, epoch challenges, and the declared fault model.
independence.holdout: F10 timing and direction are selected after development thresholds are frozen but before the independent auditor receives any bundle.
independence.antiLeakage: Event labels and operational ledgers remain hidden until the auditor has committed certificate verdicts and raw hashes.

success: Every accepted certificate identifies one event count in all admissible worlds under the declared fault budget; all injected out-of-model common-cause cases are rejected or marked inconclusive rather than misclassified.
rejection: One accepted certificate has a wrong event count, one stale or reset claim passes freshness/retention checks, or one claimed-independent witness pair shares an undeclared power, clock, processor, storage, calibration, or attack domain.
stop: Stop on unsafe motion, unbounded calibration drift, unsealed raw data, auditor leakage, dropped fault rows, or any attempt to call emulated files physical measurements.
